If you are unsure if your origin or destination is inside the strict ADA area, please contact the RAMP office at 859-814-2135

The regional paratransit application says Northern Kentucky applicants must attend an in-person assessment, with transport to it provided by the local transit provider. Bring valid photo ID and any mobility device you use; call 859-814-2135 to schedule and submit the application.

If you live in Hamilton County, Ohio, or Northern Kentucky, you will be required to complete an in-person assessment. Transportation to the assessment location will be provided by your local transit provider. You must bring a valid photo identification card and if you utilize a mobility device, you must bring it as well to your in-person assessment.
Northern Kentucky residents o Call (859) 814-2135 to schedule an assessment and submit your application.
The regional paratransit application offers help completing the form and alternative formats, including large print or a different language. It says all sections must be completed.
If you have questions, need help filling out this application, or need an alternative format (large print or in a different language), we can help you. All sections must be completed.
The regional application says applicants may be asked for a clinical professional’s assessment form. Confirm which paperwork is needed for your application.
You may be asked to have a clinical professional complete an assessment form for you.

The regional application describes a written decision within 21 days after the assessment is completed. It says the decision letter identifies any eligibility conditions and whether a personal care attendant is approved for travel; approval should not be assumed before that decision.

All applications for ADA paratransit service eligibility will be processed within 21 days from the date that the assessment is completed. Staff will notify the applicant in writing of the determination decision. The letter will state if the applicant has been approved for service, the conditions of eligibility (if any) and if a Personal Care Attendant (PCA) is approved for travel as well.
TANK Plus permits a booking for up to four people in total, including the person booking. That person pays the total fare; this is a Plus group-booking rule, not a RAMP attendant entitlement.
You may schedule a ride for up to four riders for each trip (yourself + 3 others). The passenger scheduling will pay the total fare price.
